intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by deletion or point mutation in the EYA1 gene (601653) on chromosome 8q13.3.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by deletion in the EYA1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region, confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region in OFC syndrome and calls OFC a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by point mutation in the EYA1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that not only major rearrangements, but also point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, can be found in patients with OFC syndrome.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a point mutation (a splice-site substitution) in EYA1 in an OFC patient and concludes that such mutations underlie OFC as well as large rearrangements. It says they 'can be found' rather than stating causation outright.

checks.claim: The EYA1 gene is located on chromosome 8q13.3.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the EYA1 gene (localised to 8q13.3)
checks.explanation: The paper places EYA1 at 8q13.3.

paragraphs.text: Otofaciocervical syndrome is a dysplasia (Estefanía et al., 2006). Pohl et al. (2013) listed its features as facial dysmorphism, external ear anomalies with preauricular pits, hearing impairment, branchial cysts or fistulas, anomalies of the vertebrae and the shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability. Neck and shoulder girdle abnormalities described by Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) included a long neck, sloping shoulders and winged scapulae. Rickard et al. (2001) noted that the disorder is clinically similar to branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome, which is also caused by mutation in EYA1.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome is a dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: The distinction between BOR and other dysplasias, such as oto-facio-cervical syndrome (OFC), is challenged
checks.explanation: The abstract names OFC as one of the 'other dysplasias'.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed facial dysmorphism as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by facial dysmorphism, external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment
checks.explanation: Facial dysmorphism is listed.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed external ear anomalies with preauricular pits as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment
checks.explanation: Listed.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed hearing impairment as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment
checks.explanation: Listed.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed branchial cysts or fistulas as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: branchial cysts or fistulas, anomalies of the vertebrae and the shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability
checks.explanation: Listed.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed anomalies of the vertebrae as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: anomalies of the vertebrae and the shoulder girdle
checks.explanation: Listed.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed anomalies of the shoulder girdle as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: anomalies of the vertebrae and the shoulder girdle
checks.explanation: Listed.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) listed mild intellectual disability as a feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: and mild intellectual disability
checks.explanation: Listed.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described a long neck as a neck abnormality in otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Distinguishing features were a long face with narrow nose, high arched palate, prominent and dysmorphic ears, long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: Long neck is listed among the features of the OFC syndrome patient.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described sloping shoulders as a shoulder girdle abnormality in otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: Sloping shoulders are listed among the features.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described winged scapulae as a shoulder girdle abnormality in otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: Winged scapulae are listed among the features.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) noted that otofaciocervical syndrome is clinically similar to branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to BOR syndrome, with clinical features in addition to those of BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome is also caused by mutation in EYA1.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the EYA1 gene (localised to 8q13.3) account for nearly 70% of BOR syndrome cases exhibiting at least three of the major features.
checks.explanation: The paper attributes BOR syndrome cases to EYA1 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Fára et al. (1967) reported a familial disorder that they termed oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia.

checks.claim: Fára et al. (1967) reported a familial disorder that they termed oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia.
checks.evidence_quote: [Familial oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia].
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied, and it names a familial disorder called oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia, which is exactly what the claim says.

paragraphs.text: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described a sporadic patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. The patient had a long neck, sloping shoulders and winged scapulae. Renal malformations were absent in this patient. The authors argued that otofaciocervical syndrome is a unique, clinically recognisable entity that should be distinguished from branchiootorenal syndrome.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) described a sporadic patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A sporadic patient with OFC syndrome is described.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: The sporadic otofaciocervical syndrome patient described by Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) had a long neck.
checks.evidence_quote: Distinguishing features were a long face with narrow nose, high arched palate, prominent and dysmorphic ears, long neck
checks.explanation: The patient had a long neck.

checks.claim: The sporadic otofaciocervical syndrome patient described by Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) had sloping shoulders.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: The patient had sloping shoulders.

checks.claim: The sporadic otofaciocervical syndrome patient described by Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) had winged scapulae.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: The patient had winged scapulae.

checks.claim: Renal malformations were absent in the sporadic otofaciocervical syndrome patient described by Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995).
checks.evidence_quote: The absence of preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, and renal malformations, and the presence of distinct facial and radiographic findings
checks.explanation: The abstract states that renal malformations were absent in the patient.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) argued that otofaciocervical syndrome is a unique, clinically recognisable entity that should be distinguished from branchiootorenal syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: markedly downward sloping shoulders in the present patient support OFC syndrome being a unique, clinically recognisable entity.
checks.explanation: The title ("supports splitting from the branchio-oto-renal syndrome") and the conclusion support distinguishing it from BOR.

paragraphs.text: Pohl et al. (2013) found that a hypofunctional PAX1 mutation causes autosomal recessively inherited otofaciocervical syndrome. This established PAX1 as a disease-causing gene for the disorder.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) found that a hypofunctional PAX1 mutation causes otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A hypofunctional PAX1 mutation causes autosomal recessively inherited otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.explanation: This is the paper's title.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome caused by the PAX1 mutation reported by Pohl et al. (2013) is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: identified only a single novel homozygous variant, c.497G>T, located in PAX1 that co-segregated with the disease in the family
checks.explanation: The family is consanguineous, the variant is homozygous, and the title says the disorder is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Pohl et al. (2013) established PAX1 as a disease-causing gene for otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: establish PAX1 as a new disease-causing gene for OFCS
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Rickard et al. (2001) found a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region on chromosome 8q13.3 in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. They concluded that otofaciocervical syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1 and that it is allelic with BOR syndrome. Their analysis also narrowed the critical region for Duane syndrome.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) found a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region on chromosome 8q13.3 in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region, confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The paper reports the large deletion in one OFC patient. The 8q13.3 location comes from the abstract's own statement of where EYA1 lies.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) concluded that otofaciocervical syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1.
checks.evidence_quote: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1
checks.explanation: The paper's title states this conclusion.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) concluded that otofaciocervical syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome
checks.explanation: The paper states this conclusion directly.

checks.claim: The analysis by Rickard et al. (2001) of the EYA1-region deletion narrowed the critical region for Duane syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: comparison of the boundaries of this large deletion with other reported rearrangements of the region reduces the critical region for Duane syndrome (an eye movement disorder) to between markers D8S553 and D8S1797, a genetic distance of approximately 1 cM.
checks.explanation: The paper states that the deletion boundaries narrowed the Duane syndrome critical region.

paragraphs.text: Estefanía et al. (2006) identified a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of the EYA1 gene in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. This showed that point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame can be found in patients with the syndrome, and not only major rearrangements.

checks.claim: Estefanía et al. (2006) identified a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of the EYA1 gene in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we show here that an OFC patient bears a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The EYA1 splice-site substitution reported by Estefanía et al. (2006) alters the EYA1 reading frame.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that not only major rearrangements, but also point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, can be found in patients with OFC syndrome.
checks.explanation: The conclusion describes the patient's mutation as a point mutation that alters the EYA1 reading frame. The abstract does not describe the transcript-level effect in detail.

checks.claim: Estefanía et al. (2006) showed that point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, and not only major rearrangements, can be found in patients with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that not only major rearrangements, but also point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, can be found in patients with OFC syndrome.
checks.explanation: The claim closely restates the abstract's conclusion.
